report.summary:
Both fixes are in. Test results: 12 passed, 1 failed.

1. Precedence (cfg/load.py): resolve() now checks the environment first, then the file, then defaults. The failing test, tests/test_load.py::test_file_pins_override_env, encodes the old behavior: its comment says ops pins values in the file so env vars can't override them. That directly conflicts with the env > file rule you asked for. I left the test alone because changing it is a product decision. If you want env > file everywhere, delete or invert that test. If ops really needs file pinning, tell me and I'll make it an explicit opt-in rather than the default.

2. Booleans (cfg/boolparse.py): parse_bool now lowercases input before matching and accepts yes/no/on/off in addition to true/false/1/0. The old code also rejected "TRUE" and "Yes" because it did not lowercase, so those now work too. All boolean tests pass.

messages.content:
Two config bugs in `cfg`:

1. `resolve` lets the config file win over environment variables. Precedence must be environment > file > defaults.
2. `parse_bool` only understands "true"/"false"/"1"/"0". It should also accept yes/no and on/off, in any case.

Can you fix both? Tests are in `tests/`.

input.command: cd /work && find . -type f -not -path '*/.git/*' | head -100 && echo --- && cat cfg/*.py 2>/dev/null | head -300
cd /work && ls -la; ls tests; for f in $(find . -name '*.py' -path '*cfg*'); do echo "== $f"; cat "$f"; done; echo; for f in tests/*; do echo "== $f"; cat "$f"; done
